answer:
The mother of Barack Obama's father (Barack Obama Sr.) was **Habiba Akumu Obama** (also known as Habiba Akumu Nyanjango).

According to the search results, she lived approximately from around 1918 to 2006 and was from Karabondi, Kenya. She was married to Onyango Obama (Barack Obama Sr.'s father), who was born around 1895 and died in 1979. 

After her husband's first wife left the family in 1945, their three children (including Baraka Hussein Obama, who later became Barack Obama Sr.) were raised by Onyango's third wife, Sarah Ogwel.

**Barack Hussein Obama** (;[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-7) born **Baraka Hussein Obama**,[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-books.google-8) 18 June 1934[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-Maraniss_p._65-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-Liberties_p._202-10)– 24 November 1982) was a Kenyan senior governmental economist and the father of Barack Obama, the 44th president of the United States. He is a central figure of his son's memoir, _Dreams from My Father_ (1995). Obama married in 1954 and had two children with his first wife, Kezia. He was selected for a special program to attend college in the United States and studied at the University of Hawaii where he met Ann Dunham, whom he married in 1961 following the conception of his son, Barack. Obama and Dunham divorced three years later.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-Cejka-11) Obama then went to Harvard University for graduate school, where he earned an MA in economics, and returned to Kenya in 1964. He saw his son Barack once more, when his son was about 10.

In late 1964, Obama married Ruth Beatrice Baker, an American woman he had met in Massachusetts. They had two sons together before separating in 1971 and divorcing in 1973. Obama first worked for an oil company, before beginning work as an economist with the Kenyan Ministry of Transport. He was promoted to senior economic analyst in the Ministry of Finance. He was among a cadre of young Kenyan men who had been educated in the West in a program supported by Tom Mboya. Obama had conflicts with Kenyan presidentJomo Kenyatta, which adversely affected his career. He was fired and blacklisted in Kenya, finding it nearly impossible to get a job. Obama was involved in three serious car accidents during his final years; he died as a result of the last one in 1982.

## Early life
Baraka Hussein Obama was born in 1934[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-Maraniss_p._65-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-Liberties_p._202-10) in Rachuonyo District[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-Oywa_2008b-12) on the shores of Lake Victoria just outside Kendu Bay, Kenya, at the time a colony and protectorate of the British Empire. He was raised in the village of [Nyang'oma Kogelo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nyang'oma_Kogelo "Nyang'oma Kogelo"), Siaya District, Nyanza Province.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-Ombuor-13) His family were members of the Luo people.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-14) His father was Onyango Obama (c.1895–1979), and his mother was Habiba Akumu Nyanjango (c.1918–2006) of Karabondi, Kenya, Onyango's second wife, with whom, in addition to Baraka, they had two daughters. After his mother left the family in 1945, the three children were raised by Onyango's third wife, Sarah Ogwel of Kogelo.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-Powell-15)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-Reitwiesner-16)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-17)

## Early life
### Religion and education
When Obama was about six years old and attending a Christian missionary school, he converted from Islam to Anglicanism when strongly encouraged by the staff, and changed his name from "Baraka" to "Barack".[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-books.google-8) He later became an atheist, contending that religion was mere superstition.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-spiritual_journey-18) While still living near Kendu Bay, Obama attended Gendia Primary School. After his family moved to Siaya District, he transferred to Ng'iya Intermediate School.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-Oywa_2008b-12) From 1950 to 1953, he studied at Maseno National School, an exclusive Anglican boarding school in Maseno.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-19) The head teacher, B.L. Bowers, described Obama in his records as "very keen, steady, trustworthy and friendly. Concentrates, reliable, and out-going."[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-Oywa_2008a-20) In 1954 at age 20, Obama married Kezia Aoko[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-21) in a tribal ceremony in Kenya. They had two children, Malik (a.k.a. Roy) and Auma.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-Foreman-22)

Her son spent much of his teenage years living with her parents in Hawaii, who helped raise him while Ann continued her work abroad.

In 1994, Ann was diagnosed with cancer. She died in Honolulu in November 1995, at the age of 52.

She never got to see what her son would become. Thirteen years later, in 2008, Barack Obama was elected President of the United States.

He has described her as the dominant figure in his formative years, and credited her with shaping his values and his belief in the dignity of all people.

Her story is a reminder that the people who shape our lives most are often the ones who quietly keep going, through hardship and uncertainty, and pour their hopes into the next generation.

Determined that he would get a good education, Ann would wake him up before dawn to give him English lessons before school. Baraka Hussein Obama was born in 1934[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-Maraniss_p._65-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-Liberties_p._202-10) in Rachuonyo District[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-Oywa_2008b-12) on the shores of Lake Victoria just outside Kendu Bay, Kenya, at the time a colony and protectorate of the British Empire. He was raised in the village of [Nyang'oma Kogelo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nyang'oma_Kogelo "Nyang'oma Kogelo"), Siaya District, Nyanza Province.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-Ombuor-13) His family were members of the Luo people.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-14) His father was Onyango Obama (c.1895–1979), and his mother was Habiba Akumu Nyanjango (c.1918–2006) of Karabondi, Kenya, Onyango's second wife, with whom, in addition to Baraka, they had two daughters. After his mother left the family in 1945, the three children were raised by Onyango's third wife, Sarah Ogwel of Kogelo.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-Powell-15)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-Reitwiesner-16)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-17)

## Early life
### Religion and education
When Obama was about six years old and attending a Christian missionary school, he converted from Islam to Anglicanism when strongly encouraged by the staff, and changed his name from "Baraka" to "Barack".[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-books.google-8) He later became an atheist, contending that religion was mere superstition.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-spiritual_journey-18) While still living near Kendu Bay, Obama attended Gendia Primary School. After his family moved to Siaya District, he transferred to Ng'iya Intermediate School.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-Oywa_2008b-12) From 1950 to 1953, he studied at Maseno National School, an exclusive Anglican boarding school in Maseno.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-19) The head teacher, B.L. Bowers, described Obama in his records as "very keen, steady, trustworthy and friendly. Concentrates, reliable, and out-going."[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-Oywa_2008a-20) In 1954 at age 20, Obama married Kezia Aoko[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-21) in a tribal ceremony in Kenya. They had two children, Malik (a.k.a. Roy) and Auma.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-Foreman-22)

# Stanley Ann Dunham was born in Wichita, Kansas, in 1942. Her father had hoped for a boy, so he gave her his own first name. Most people knew her simply as Ann. In 1960, while studying at the University of Hawaii, she met Barack Obama Sr., a student from Kenya, in a Russian language class. In February 1961, they married. At the time, interracial marriage was still illegal in many US states. That August, at just 18 years old, Ann gave birth to a son. Life wasn’t easy. She spent time as a young single mother, studying in Seattle while caring for her baby. Later she returned to Hawaii, went back to university, and in 1964, at 21, filed for divorce. But she kept going. She finished her degree, remarried, and in 1967 moved to Jakarta, Indonesia, with her young son. Determined that he would get a good education, Ann would wake him up before dawn to give him English lessons before school. When he complained, according to his memoir, she reminded him that it was no picnic for her either. Over the years, she built a career as an anthropologist, working in Indonesia on projects to support rural communities and small businesses. In 1992, she earned her PhD, with a study of village blacksmiths in Indonesia. Her son spent much of his teenage years living with her parents in Hawaii, who helped raise him while Ann continued her work abroad. In 1994, Ann was diagnosed with cancer. She died in Honolulu in November 1995, at the age of 52. She never got to see what her son would become. Thirteen years later, in 2008, Barack Obama was elected President of the United States. He has described her as the dominant figure in his formative years, and credited her with shaping his values and his belief in the dignity of all people. Her story is a reminder that the people who shape our lives most are often the ones who quietly keep going, through hardship and uncertainty, and pour their hopes into the next generation. **Barack Hussein Obama** (;[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-7) born **Baraka Hussein Obama**,[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-books.google-8) 18 June 1934[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-Maraniss_p._65-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-Liberties_p._202-10)– 24 November 1982) was a Kenyan senior governmental economist and the father of Barack Obama, the 44th president of the United States. He is a central figure of his son's memoir, _Dreams from My Father_ (1995). Obama married in 1954 and had two children with his first wife, Kezia. He was selected for a special program to attend college in the United States and studied at the University of Hawaii where he met Ann Dunham, whom he married in 1961 following the conception of his son, Barack. Obama and Dunham divorced three years later.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-Cejka-11) Obama then went to Harvard University for graduate school, where he earned an MA in economics, and returned to Kenya in 1964. He saw his son Barack once more, when his son was about 10.

In late 1964, Obama married Ruth Beatrice Baker, an American woman he had met in Massachusetts. They had two sons together before separating in 1971 and divorcing in 1973. Obama first worked for an oil company, before beginning work as an economist with the Kenyan Ministry of Transport. He was promoted to senior economic analyst in the Ministry of Finance. He was among a cadre of young Kenyan men who had been educated in the West in a program supported by Tom Mboya. Obama had conflicts with Kenyan presidentJomo Kenyatta, which adversely affected his career. He was fired and blacklisted in Kenya, finding it nearly impossible to get a job. Obama was involved in three serious car accidents during his final years; he died as a result of the last one in 1982.

The mother of Barack Obama's father (Barack Obama Sr.) was **Habiba Akumu Obama** (also known as Habiba Akumu Nyanjango).

According to the search results, she lived approximately from around 1918 to 2006 and was from Karabondi, Kenya. She was married to Onyango Obama (Barack Obama Sr.'s father), who was born around 1895 and died in 1979. 

After her husband's first wife left the family in 1945, their three children (including Baraka Hussein Obama, who later became Barack Obama Sr.) were raised by Onyango's third wife, Sarah Ogwel.
